newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels destroy refugee ship.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels destroy refugee ship.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists on Tuesday forcibly boarded a ship used to ferry refugees in northwestern Sri Lanka and destroyed it by setting it on fire, naval officials said.

They said five Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) boats attacked the passenger ship at Pesalai in northwestern Mannar, some 240 km (150 miles) north of the capital Colombo and abducted the crew before setting the ship on fire.
Only the crew was on board when the ship was attacked by the rebels at 6.30 a.m. (1200 GMT), the officials said.

"It was a private ship which could carry 250 passengers. But at the time of the attack only the crew was on board since it was coming to Mannar to take refugees to Jaffna peninsula," a navy official told Reuters.
Officials said the ship, named Misen, which was anchored some distance off Pesalai, had a crew of nine including two Indonesians, one of whom was the captain and the other the chief engineer.
"The captain was supposed to have handed over his charge to somebody else, so we are not sure whether he was still on the ship," a navy spokesman said, adding the crew's whereabouts was not known.
No further details were immediately available.
The ship, which had been leased by Sri Lanka's rehabilitation ministry from a private company to ferry refugees to northern Jaffna peninsula from Mannar, had been gutted by fire, navy officials said.
An LTTE spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
Government troops launched a major offensive on the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold in May to open a strategic highway linking northern Jaffna peninsula to rest of the island.
The offensive has slowed after rebels launched two counter-attacks last month, in which scores of soldiers and separatists were reportedly killed.
Independent confirmation of the events is not possible because journalists are not allowed in the war zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
